philosophy.strictness: A test should fail on a missing expected finding or an unexpected extra finding.
philosophy.escape_invalidation: Any user-modifiable hook/filter after an escaping operation invalidates the escaping guarantee for subsequent output.
philosophy.database_boundary: Stored data must be treated as untrusted again when read for output, even if it was sanitized on input.

scenarios.title: Direct POST to option
scenarios.purpose: Basic superglobal source and storage boundary.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Raw POST data is written to an option. wp_unslash() changes slashing, not trust.
scenarios.safe_reason: The value is unslashed and sanitized with sanitize_text_field() before storage.

scenarios.title: Nested settings array
scenarios.purpose: Array taint must survive nesting and whole-array assignment.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A nested POST array is written wholesale to an option without recursively sanitizing values.
scenarios.safe_reason: map_deep() applies sanitize_text_field() recursively before storage.

scenarios.title: Numeric GET parameter
scenarios.purpose: Context-specific scalar validation/casting.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A request value expected to be an integer reaches post meta unchanged.
scenarios.safe_reason: absint() validates/coerces the numeric identifier before storage.

scenarios.title: Uploaded filename
scenarios.purpose: File metadata is user-controlled input.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: The original upload name is persisted without filename sanitisation.
scenarios.safe_reason: sanitize_file_name() is applied before writing the filename to metadata.

scenarios.title: REST request parameter
scenarios.purpose: Framework object methods can be taint sources.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: WP_REST_Request::get_param() is treated as untrusted and written to user meta directly.
scenarios.safe_reason: sanitize_textarea_field() runs before the write.

scenarios.title: Shortcode attribute persisted
scenarios.purpose: shortcode_atts() supplies defaults but is not a sanitizer.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A shortcode attribute is persisted as a CSS class without sanitisation.
scenarios.safe_reason: sanitize_html_class() constrains the class before storage.

scenarios.title: Cookie to option
scenarios.purpose: Cookies are attacker-controlled request data too.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A cookie value is written directly to an option.
scenarios.safe_reason: sanitize_key() constrains the expected token-like value before storage.

scenarios.title: Remote HTTP body to option
scenarios.purpose: Third-party responses are untrusted input, even without a browser request.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Remote HTML is persisted without constraining allowed markup.
scenarios.safe_reason: wp_kses_post() constrains the remote HTML before it is stored.

scenarios.title: Option in HTML text
scenarios.purpose: Database reads remain untrusted for output.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: An option value is echoed inside element text without escaping.
scenarios.safe_reason: esc_html() is applied at the output boundary.

scenarios.title: Post meta in attribute
scenarios.purpose: Attribute context requires attribute escaping.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Post meta is interpolated into a class attribute raw.
scenarios.safe_reason: esc_attr() is used at the attribute sink.

scenarios.title: User meta in URL attribute
scenarios.purpose: URL context requires URL escaping, not generic text escaping.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: User meta is used directly as an href.
scenarios.safe_reason: esc_url() is applied at the href output boundary.

scenarios.title: add_query_arg URL output
scenarios.purpose: URL construction is not output escaping.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A URL built with add_query_arg() from the current request is emitted without esc_url().
scenarios.safe_reason: The final URL is escaped with esc_url() at the href sink.
scenarios.inspiration: CVE-2024-8730 and similar add_query_arg reflected-XSS reports

scenarios.title: Allowed rich HTML
scenarios.purpose: Intentional HTML needs KSES-style output handling.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Stored rich text is echoed verbatim.
scenarios.safe_reason: wp_kses_post() permits post-safe markup while removing disallowed HTML.

scenarios.title: Inline JavaScript string
scenarios.purpose: Output escaping is context-specific for JavaScript.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Stored data is concatenated into an inline JS string literal raw.
scenarios.safe_reason: esc_js() is applied to the dynamic string at the JavaScript sink.

scenarios.title: Textarea context
scenarios.purpose: Textarea output has its own escaping helper.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Stored data is emitted directly between textarea tags.
scenarios.safe_reason: esc_textarea() is applied at the output boundary.

scenarios.title: XML context
scenarios.purpose: XML output should not be treated like plain HTML text.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A stored URL is placed into an XML element raw.
scenarios.safe_reason: esc_xml() is applied at the XML sink.

scenarios.title: Wrong-context escape
scenarios.purpose: An escape is not universally valid across sink contexts.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: esc_html() is used for an href value; the value is escaped, but with the wrong semantic/context helper.
scenarios.safe_reason: esc_url() is used for the URL attribute.

scenarios.title: Escape invalidated by filter
scenarios.purpose: The suite-specific late-escaping invariant: a filter after escaping invalidates safety.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: The value is escaped, then passed through apply_filters(), which can replace or append arbitrary data before echo.
scenarios.safe_reason: The filter runs first and esc_html() is the final transformation before output.

scenarios.title: Reflected request to HTML text
scenarios.purpose: The smallest end-to-end source-to-sink flow.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A GET parameter reaches HTML text with neither input sanitisation nor output escaping.
scenarios.safe_reason: sanitize_text_field() is used on input and esc_html() is used at output.

scenarios.title: Stored settings XSS
scenarios.purpose: A complete request → database → later output path.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Raw POST data is stored, later read back, and echoed unescaped.
scenarios.safe_reason: Input is sanitized before storage and escaped again at the later output boundary.

scenarios.title: Shortcode attribute to class
scenarios.purpose: Real-world shortcode XSS family.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A user-controlled shortcode attribute flows through shortcode_atts() and into an HTML class attribute.
scenarios.safe_reason: The class is sanitized and escaped in the attribute context.
scenarios.inspiration: CVE-2025-12661 / CVE-2025-14109 style shortcode-attribute stored XSS

scenarios.title: Request URI through add_query_arg
scenarios.purpose: CVE-shaped reflected URL flow.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: REQUEST_URI propagates through add_query_arg() into an href without URL escaping.
scenarios.safe_reason: The composed URL is escaped only after all query-string construction is complete.
scenarios.inspiration: CVE-2024-8730 and multiple similar WordPress plugin CVEs

scenarios.title: AJAX setting with nonce
scenarios.purpose: Security checks do not sanitize payloads.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A valid nonce is checked, but raw AJAX POST data is still stored and later echoed raw. The nonce must not clear taint.
scenarios.safe_reason: Nonce verification remains, while the value is sanitized on input and escaped on output.

scenarios.title: REST to post meta to block render
scenarios.purpose: Framework callbacks and delayed rendering.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A REST parameter is stored in post meta and later rendered by a dynamic block callback without escaping.
scenarios.safe_reason: The REST value is sanitized before storage and escaped in the block renderer.

scenarios.title: Custom class propagation
scenarios.purpose: Taint should survive ordinary user-defined method calls.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Request data passes through getter and normalizer methods; trim/strtolower do not sanitize it before output.
scenarios.safe_reason: The source is sanitized in the boundary method and escaped at output.

scenarios.title: Array merge and nested access
scenarios.purpose: Array reconstruction must not accidentally drop taint.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: POST data is merged into a new array, stored, retrieved, and one nested element is output raw.
scenarios.safe_reason: The merged structure is recursively sanitized and the retrieved value is escaped at output.
scenarios.inspiration: Psalm issue #10919 demonstrates why reconstructed/nested arrays deserve explicit taint regressions

scenarios.title: Conditional merge
scenarios.purpose: A tainted branch must taint the merged value.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: The default is trusted, but one control-flow branch assigns raw request data before the common sink.
scenarios.safe_reason: The request branch sanitizes its value and output is escaped.

scenarios.title: sprintf and concatenation
scenarios.purpose: Formatted strings are propagators, not sanitizers.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A request value flows into sprintf(), then the assembled HTML is echoed.
scenarios.safe_reason: The dynamic value is sanitized and escaped at the point it enters the HTML template.

scenarios.title: Plugin filter to theme sink
scenarios.purpose: Cross-component flow through WordPress filters.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A plugin injects request data into a filter; a theme applies the filter and echoes the result raw.
scenarios.safe_reason: The plugin sanitizes its request value and, critically, the theme escapes after apply_filters().

scenarios.title: Sanitized storage, unsafe theme output
scenarios.purpose: Sanitization and escaping are independent guarantees.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A plugin correctly sanitizes before storage, but the theme assumes stored data is safe and echoes it raw.
scenarios.safe_reason: The theme still escapes the database value at output.

scenarios.title: Raw storage, safely escaped theme
scenarios.purpose: Safe output must not hide a bad input boundary.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: The theme escapes correctly, but a plugin writes raw request data to persistent storage. The input violation should still be reported.
scenarios.safe_reason: The plugin sanitizes before storage; the theme continues to escape at output.

scenarios.title: Escaped plugin value invalidated by another plugin
scenarios.purpose: The core custom invariant across plugin boundaries.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Plugin A escapes a value, then exposes it to a filter. Plugin B appends request data. The theme echoes the returned value, so the original escape is no longer a valid guarantee.
scenarios.safe_reason: Plugins return/filter data first; the theme performs the final esc_html() immediately before output.

scenarios.title: Filter replaces escaped value
scenarios.purpose: A filter can replace, not merely append to, an escaped value.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: The theme escapes a default value before apply_filters(); another plugin completely replaces it with stored data, then the theme echoes it.
scenarios.safe_reason: The filtered value is escaped only after all callbacks have completed.

scenarios.title: Global state across action boundary
scenarios.purpose: Cross-file globals and action callbacks can carry taint.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: A plugin copies POST data into a global. The theme triggers an action whose plugin callback echoes the global raw.
scenarios.safe_reason: The value is sanitized when captured and escaped inside the output callback.

scenarios.title: Remote response through filter to rich HTML
scenarios.purpose: External content, filters, and HTML-preserving escaping.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Remote HTML flows through a filter and is output directly. The filter means any earlier assumptions about the remote body are insufficient.
scenarios.safe_reason: Filtering happens first, then wp_kses_post() is the final output transformation.

scenarios.title: Inline script JSON boundary
scenarios.purpose: Structured encoding versus raw JavaScript concatenation.
scenarios.vulnerable_issue: Request data is concatenated into inline JavaScript passed to wp_add_inline_script().
scenarios.safe_reason: The input is sanitized and wp_json_encode() is used to create a JavaScript literal before the inline-script sink.
